cards.meaning: [ is a synonym for test (builtin); compares expressions / file tests and returns an exit status
cards.example:
test -f file.txt && echo "File exists"
[ -f file.txt ] && echo Indeed
cards.notes: Status 0 = true, 1 = false. Spaces inside the brackets: [ -f file.txt ].

cards.meaning: If the last command failed, do this
cards.notes: $? is the exit status of the previous command.

cards.meaning: EXPRESSION is true (grouping inside test / [ ])
cards.notes: Often need \( \) with [ so the shell does not treat ( ) specially.

cards.meaning: EXPRESSION is false — negate the test
AND inside test / [ ]
OR inside test / [ ]
The length of STRING is nonzero (non-empty)
The length of STRING is zero (empty)
FILE exists and is a directory
FILE exists and is a regular file
FILE exists and write permission is granted
Extended test — a keyword (not a command); Bash sees it as one element that returns an exit status
cards.notes: Bash 2.02+. Safer with spaces than [ ]. Prevents many logic errors.

cards.meaning: These operators work inside [[ ]] but error inside [ ]
[ word-splits an unquoted value (too many arguments); [[ treats it as one test
cards.example:
string_with_spaces='some spaces here'
[ -n $string_with_spaces ]  →  [: too many arguments
cards.notes: Classic reason to prefer [[ ]] for string tests.

cards.meaning: String match against a glob pattern inside [[ ]]
Regex match inside [[ ]]
cards.notes: =~ is the regex operator in extended test.

cards.meaning: Arithmetic evaluation that returns an exit status from the numeric value
cards.notes: Non-zero value → status 0 (true). Zero value → status 1 (false). See man bash ARITHMETIC EVALUATION.

cards.meaning: Run the then-branch when a list of commands returns status 0
cards.example:
if [ condition1 ]; then
  command1
elif [ condition2 ]; then
  command4
else
  default-command
fi
cards.notes: fi is if backwards. Can test any command, not only brackets.

cards.meaning: if tests a command list — not only [ ] / [[ ]]
cards.notes: Status 0 for the whole list → then-branch.

cards.meaning: Match EXPRESSION against patterns; run the matching clause
cards.notes: Each clause ends with ;;. esac is case backwards.

cards.meaning: Default case arm — matches anything not already matched
AND list — each command runs only if the previous returned true (0)
cards.notes: First failure stops the chain. Can replace nested if/then.

cards.meaning: OR list — each command runs only while the previous returned false
